newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan guerrilla said to give Taleban 19 Stingers.
newsitem.headline: Afghan guerrilla said to give Taleban 19 Stingers.

text.p: An Afghan guerrilla has given 19 U.S.-made Stinger anti-aircraft missiles to the radical Islamic Taleban militia, a Taleban spokesman said on Wednesday.

The spokesman, Abdul Ghafoor, told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press agency that a guerrilla named Mohammad Hassan had handed over the Stingers to the Taleban in the town of Sarobi, 70 km (45 miles) east of Kabul, on Tuesday.
"Hassan is a righteous man and that is why he gave the missiles to the Taleban," Ghafoor said.
He said Hassan was a member of ousted Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami faction, driven from Sarobi by the Taleban during their march on Kabul last month.
Ghafoor said Hezb-i-Islami had previously assigned Hassan the task of collecting Stingers from different groups.

A senior Islamabad-based Hezb-i-Islami leader, Ghairat Baheer, dismissed the report as baseless. "We have no commander by this name and the Stingers were given to individual commanders, not to parties," he told Reuters.

Stingers were used to lethal effect against Soviet aircraft during the occupation of Afghanistan in the 1980s. The United States tried to recover unused stocks after the Soviet withdrawal, but Afghans with Stingers guarded them jealously.
